videos.script: Two study sessions. Same course, same minutes, same day. Are they equal? Without one word, Kotlin says no, and a set happily holds both. {{data}} That word is data. Put it in front of class, and the compiler writes the functions a value needs. A readable toString. Equals and hashCode that compare what is inside. {{eq}} Then the difference between two equals signs and three: equal values, or the very same object. {{copy}} Copy, which changes a value without changing it. And the trap in it: a copy is shallow. {{destructure}} Destructuring, which takes an object apart by position, and why the names you write on the left do not matter at all. {{limits}} What a data class leaves out. {{value}} And value classes, which give one number a type of its own, so seconds can no longer be passed where minutes are expected.
